items.title: Roy McCurdy interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: That was one we were doing for Capitol Records in Los Angeles... Cannon's recording... We were recording... Cannon called them both up... Joe would hit it... after Cannon left

ctx.x: That was one we were doing for Capitol Records in Los Angeles. We were doing a live recording. What they used to do at Capitol is they used to take the big studio, I think it was A studio, it’s huge. And they’d make it into a night club. They’d put a bar in there, drinks, and they’d call people and tell them Cannon’s recording. Well I mean, by the time we did our third album I mean there was hundreds, I mean there was just a crowd outside the Capitol Records, you know, trying to get in for this thing. But we were…

They sure did. There was some very great piano players too, with the band of course. When tunes like “Mercy, Mercy” and stuff, when — you would read them in rehearsal, did you get a sense of — this tune is going to sell a lot of records?
